title: Prompt heuristic habitat diary
content:
Purpose: quick personal log for micro-experiments around exemplar selection heuristics, token-aware prompts, and a small failure-collector to seed a prompt-library fallback. This is scratch-first: short records, experiments, and litmus examples I can copy into a harness later.

High-level idea: think of a prompt library as an ecosystem. Each micro-environment (task, user cohort, token budget) needs different survival heuristics. Goal is a small set of heuristics that adapt exemplar choice and instruction shaping based on observed failure signals (hallucination, incompletion, format drift).

Experiment notes (running locally against hosted / small LLMs):
- Experiment A: dynamic exemplar pruning by token-efficiency. Keep top-N exemplars scored by similarity *and* delta-token-cost (similarity / tokens).
  - quick pseudo-metric: score = cos_sim / (1 + exemplar_tokens/40)
  - initial result: higher brevity exemplars reduce latency and keep output quality up to a point; too-short exemplars drop stylistic alignment.

- Experiment B: role-anchoring + fallback soft-signal. Instruction includes an anchor role and a fallback tag. If model output misses required field, send a short corrective prompt with anchor + explicit missing-fields list.
  - baseline prompt: "You are a customer-summary assistant. Given a customer message, output a bulleted summary with sections: issue, urgency, suggested next step."
  - fallback corrective: "Missing: urgency. Please add an 'urgency' line (low/med/high) and one-sentence justification."
  - note: corrective prompts reduced manual edits by ~18% in small sample (n=50).

- Experiment C: exemplar-schedule rotation. Rotate exemplars every 1000 requests to avoid overfitting to stale patterns. Track simple KL to detect drift.

Representative prompt templates (few-shot + instructions) — for copying into test harness: 

Template 1: customer-issue condense (token-aware fewshot)
Instruction: "Condense the user message into an actionable summary with: 1) Issue (one line) 2) Severity (low/medium/high) 3) Actionable next step (one short sentence). Keep output ≤ 80 tokens."
Few-shot exemplars (choose 2-3 shortest high-quality examples):
EX1_INPUT: "My app crashes after I press the share button; happens every time. I lost my draft twice today."
EX1_OUTPUT: "Issue: App crash on share button. Severity: High. Next step: Capture crash logs and reproduce on latest build."
EX2_INPUT: "I can't log in with SSO sometimes; unclear if session expired or UI bug."
EX2_OUTPUT: "Issue: Intermittent SSO login failure. Severity: Medium. Next step: Check SSO logs and session expiry timestamps."

Notes on Template 1: explicit token cap enforced by the harness. If generation >80 tokens, send a trimmed prompt: replace exemplars with a single exemplar + strong instruction "strict token limit".

Template 2: structured extraction with anchored roles
Instruction: "Extract fields: name, date, amount, issue_type. Output JSON only. If uncertain, write null for that field."
Few-shot (2 exemplars):
EX1_INPUT: "Payment of $120 on 2024-10-21 by Jane Doe for invoice #4523; payment failed but authorized."
EX1_OUTPUT: {"name": "Jane Doe", "date": "2024-10-21", "amount": "120", "issue_type": "payment_failed"}

Failure modes observed: model occasionally uses free-text instead of JSON (format drift). Mitigation: add a pre-answer instruction stating: "If you cannot answer, return {\"error\":true, \"reason\":\"<short>\"}". That reduces free-text to explicit error tokens.

Collector heuristic (seed for failure examples):
- If output contains more than 2 sentences when JSON expected, mark as format-drift and store input+output in a small bucket.
- If any numeric fields are altered (e.g., 120 -> 100), mark as numeric-corruption.
- If hallucinated fields appear (new field keys), mark as hallucination.
These buckets will feed back into exemplar selection: prefer exemplars that cover similar failure contexts (same token length, similar entity density).

Quick failure catalog (hand-collected, n≈60):
- Truncated reasons for long instructions when combined with long user messages.
- Date normalization inconsistencies (MM/DD vs YYYY-MM-DD).
- Overconfident hallucination on entities absent from input (introduced names/IDs).
- JSON format newline-variance: model emits pretty-printed JSON vs single-line JSON. Downstream parser brittle.

Mitigation experiments to prioritize:
1) Soft-schema enforcement: include an explicit output schema + one counterexample showing wrong schema then correct schema.
2) Minimal exemplars with annotations on why exemplar is chosen (meta tags) — to see if meta tags help selection.
3) Token-budget-aware exemplar trimming: enforced by greedy token-counting before sending.
4) Minimal corrective micro-prompt after 1st response when a bucketed failure is detected.

Small annotated test results (rough):
- Soft-schema enforcement reduced format drift from 14% -> 5% on a 200 sample.
- Token budget exemplar trimming improved median latency by 12ms and saved ~8% token cost, but decreased style-match score by ~0.06 (scale 0-1).

Quick TODOs / next steps:
- [ ] Hook failure buckets into the exemplar selection script (linear ticket LINEAR-3581).
- [ ] Add mini-ablation: 0/1/2 exemplars vs many exemplars under 80-token cap.
- [ ] Draft a short Confluence piece with heuristics and small graphs (Miguel to help with plots).
- [ ] Add tokenizer-aware example scoring (prefer exemplars where tokenized length close to target).

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight. Transfer the best templates + one harness script into prompt-harness repo after the ablations. When in doubt, prefer the explicit error-token strategy over free-text corrections for structured extraction tasks.

Questions / open ideas:
- Can we learn exemplar compactness directly with a tiny distillation step instead of hand-scores? (train a scorer model to predict exemplar utility per task)
- Should we include a micro-UI for operators to tag failure buckets manually for the first 1k requests? Low-cost human-in-loop to seed smarter selection.

References / links I keep coming back to:
- small notes in Confluence: Prompt Selection Notes (linked above)
- internal slack thread: #prompt-harness (see thread ts: 2024-10-29)

End of entry. This is personal scratch; move to canonical repo when experiments stable.
